What we confirmed on official pages

  • Tax calendar: county mails valuation notices March 1 (K.S.A. 79-1460); equalization appeal due 30 days from notice mailing date (79-1448); informal meeting with County Appraiser by May 15; Hearing Officer/Panel hearings by July 1 (79-1606)
  • Late interest on real property (K.S.A. 79-2004) for 2017 and after is the K.S.A. 79-2968 prescribed rate plus five percentage points; page's personal-property rate table lists 2025 9% and 2026 8%
  • Unpaid delinquent personal property tax blocks vehicle tag renewal
  • Appeal of valuation notice due 30 days from date county mailed notice (K.S.A. 79-1448); informal meeting by May 15; hearing officer/panel hearings by July 1; then 30 days from informal/panel decision to file with state tax appeals/small claims (page labels it Small Claims Division, 79-1606)

What we could not confirm

  • Treasurer office hours not on page scraped
  • Current 2026 real property interest percentage (formula plus 5 points; exact figure not shown for real property)

Sedgwick County by the numbers

What is Sedgwick County, Kansas, and who lives there?

Sedgwick County is the second most populous county in Kansas, with Wichita as its county seat. The 2020 census counted 523,824 residents, and the 2025 estimate listed on Wikipedia is 538,433.

The county was founded in 1867 and named for John Sedgwick, a Union general killed in the Civil War. It covers 1,009 square miles, with only about 12 of them water, and borders Harvey, Butler, Cowley, Sumner, Kingman and Reno counties.

ItemDetail
County seatWichita
Area1,009 sq mi total, 998 land
Population, 2020 census523,824
EstablishedFebruary 26, 1867
Metro areaPart of the Wichita metropolitan statistical area
Area code316

Source for the table: Wikipedia's county article, which cites the Census Bureau.

Which cities and school districts sit inside Sedgwick County?

The county has twenty cities, from Wichita down to Viola. Besides Wichita they include Andale, Bel Aire, Bentley, Cheney, Clearwater, Colwich, Derby, Eastborough, Garden Plain, Goddard, Haysville, Kechi, Maize, Mount Hope, Mulvane, Park City, Sedgwick and Valley Center.

School district lines do not follow city limits closely, and Wikipedia lists twenty districts that serve parts of the county. Wichita USD 259, Derby USD 260, Haysville USD 261, Valley Center USD 262, Mulvane USD 263, Clearwater USD 264, Goddard USD 265 and Maize USD 266 are some of the larger names. The Air Force housing office also names Andover USD 385, Mulvane, Haysville, Maize and Goddard as districts around McConnell Air Force Base, with Derby USD 260 serving base family housing.

Your tax statement is the best way to learn which district you are in, because the school levy is a large part of the bill. Two houses on the same street can occasionally belong to different districts.

What does the Sedgwick County economy look like?

Aviation is the best known industry. Wikipedia credits Sedgwick County as the home of Cessna and Learjet, and the same article names White Castle and Pizza Hut as restaurant brands that began here.

Derby shows how that works locally. The city, a southern suburb of Wichita with 25,625 residents in 2020, stayed largely rural until after World War II. Wikipedia says the aviation industry and McConnell Air Force Base then drove a Cold War boom. The base took its name in April 1954 from two of the three Flying McConnell brothers of Wichita, according to the Air Force.

Transportation helps explain where people live. Interstate 35, which is the Kansas Turnpike, I-135 and I-235 cross the county, along with US 54 and US 400, US 81 and several state highways. Wichita Transit provides bus service, and Wichita Dwight D. Eisenhower National Airport is the county's main commercial airport.

How does the Sedgwick County Appraiser notify owners and take appeals?

The County Appraiser mails real property valuation notices on March 1. If you did not get yours, the office says you can view and print it online, and the printed copy shows the appeal information.

You may appeal your value once per tax year. The informal appeal form on the back of the notice must come back within 30 days, typically by March 31. The office then schedules an appointment by telephone or in person, and mails the date about ten days before. Informal appeals also run in May and December.

If the informal meeting does not settle things, the next step is the Board of Tax Appeals Small Claims Division, available for a single-family residence or for non-agricultural property valued below $3 million. Filing fees may apply. A representative who is not the owner, an immediate relative or an attorney needs a declaration of representative form.

  • General appeal documents go to ApprHear@sedgwick.gov.
  • Commercial appeals go to ApprCom@sedgwick.gov.
  • The office recommends that you submit evidence such as comparable sales, photos and repair estimates.

What are the Sedgwick County tax and appeal dates?

The county posts a statutory calendar with the dates below. A deadline that lands on a weekend or holiday moves to the next business day.

EventDateK.S.A.
Valuation notices mailedMarch 179-1460
Equalization appeal30 days from mailing79-1448
Informal meeting with appraiserMay 1579-1448
Appraiser final determinationMay 2079-1448
Appraiser certifies values to ClerkJune 179-1466
Hearing officer or panel hearingsJuly 179-1606
County Clerk certifies tax roll to TreasurerNovember 179-1803
Tax statements mailedDecember 1579-2001
Full or first half dueDecember 2079-2004
Second half dueMay 1079-2004

Local governments certify budgets to the County Clerk by August 25, which is why final levies come late in the year. The Kansas Department of Revenue says you can also file a payment under protest form with the treasurer when you pay.

What happens when Sedgwick County property tax goes unpaid?

Unpaid real estate tax can end in a tax foreclosure auction. The Treasurer's page says K.S.A. 79-2801 requires counties to foreclose on and sell, by public auction, real estate that carries delinquent tax liens.

The Treasurer's office selects parcels whose taxes are two and a half or three and a half years delinquent. The 2026 notice said that, to stay off the list, owners had to pay through the 2022 tax year, or 2023 for lots. On October 1, 2026 a first foreclosure fee of $400 was added to each parcel. The 2026 auction has been held, and cases for 2027 will be posted on the same page.

  • Once a case is filed in District Court, redemption requires payment in cash or certified funds for all delinquent years, interest and fees.
  • Owners, heirs and lienholders of record can redeem through close of business the day before the sale.
  • A private sale before the auction is a deal between you and the buyer. Recording a new deed does not stop the proceedings, but payment in full does.
  • After a sale, owners or lienholders can challenge it in District Court.
  • Auction buyers owe the full tax for the year of sale and any special assessments, but not the delinquent taxes, and a $21 deed filing fee is due at checkout.
  • Deeds usually arrive about 120 days after the sale, and the county is not responsible for evicting occupants.

Delinquent amounts for each month are valid if paid by 5 p.m. on the 20th, and interest is added after that. Separately, unpaid personal property tax blocks vehicle tag renewal, and a court warrant can follow if it is still unpaid by October 20.

How does a sale get recorded in Sedgwick County?

The deed is filed with the Register of Deeds, and a Kansas Real Estate Sales Validation Questionnaire must be filed with it. After the deed is filed, the County Clerk records the transfer for taxation and keeps the owner's mailing address in the tax system.

The Register of Deeds advises talking to a real estate attorney or title company about which deed form suits your sale. The county's contact numbers are 316-660-9400 for the Register of Deeds, 316-660-9200 for the County Clerk, and 316-660-9000 for the Treasurer.

Check special assessments with the County Clerk or your city clerk before closing. They are tracked separately from the general levy, and the county's foreclosure page tells bidders to look into them.

Which Sedgwick County sellers run into trouble?

The county's own notices point to a few situations that cause trouble. Houses with several years of delinquent tax are the most urgent, since the foreclosure clock runs on the two and a half and three and a half year marks. Inherited houses are another group, because the Treasurer's redemption rules name heirs among the parties who can redeem.

Owners who miss the 30-day informal appeal window also have fewer options for that tax year, since a value can be appealed only once per tax year.

  • Pull the delinquent balance from the Treasurer before you set a price.
  • Ask whether special assessments are attached to the parcel.
  • Decide early whether to appeal the notice, because the appeal is limited to one per tax year.

If you want to talk through a sale, send us the address of your Sedgwick County house and we will tell you what a cash offer could involve.

More questions about Sedgwick County, KS Property Tax Guide

Where do I appeal a Sedgwick County property valuation?

Start with the Sedgwick County Appraiser's Office. The informal appeal form on the back of your March 1 notice must be returned within 30 days, usually by March 31.

When is Sedgwick County property tax due?

Full payment or the first half is due December 20, and the second half is due May 10. The Treasurer mails statements by December 15.

How long can taxes go unpaid before foreclosure in Sedgwick County?

The Treasurer selects parcels that are two and a half or three and a half years delinquent. Unredeemed properties go to auction after a District Court case.

Can I sell my Sedgwick County house if taxes are delinquent?

Yes. Payment in full stops the foreclosure process, and a sale that pays the balance at closing does that. Recording a deed alone does not stop the case.

What forms are filed when a Sedgwick County house sells?

A deed goes to the Register of Deeds with a Kansas Real Estate Sales Validation Questionnaire. The County Clerk then updates the tax record.

Who to contact in Johnson County

  • Johnson County Treasury

What we confirmed on official pages

  • Pay in full by Dec. 20 or in two installments: first half by Dec. 20, second half by May 10 of following year; first notices mailed mid-November, second notices beginning of April
  • Payments after due date are late and subject to interest (K.S.A. 79-2004); failure to receive a statement does not waive interest; no rate percentage given on page

Johnson County by the numbers

Where is Johnson County, Kansas, and what is in it?

Johnson County's county seat is Olathe. The county government says its 476 square miles were once part of the Shawnee Indian Reservation, opened to settlement in 1854, and the Kansas Territorial Legislature created the county on August 25, 1855.

The Census Bureau puts the July 2025 population estimate at 636,906, with about 1,288 people per square mile in 2020. The Kansas Department of Commerce lists Overland Park, Olathe, Shawnee, Lenexa, Leawood, Prairie Village, Gardner, Merriam and Mission as the major cities.

That mix matters when you sell. A house in Overland Park and a house in Gardner share one county appraiser and one treasurer, but they sit in different city, school and special taxing districts, so two neighbors a few miles apart can pay quite different bills on similar values.

What does the Johnson County economy look like for a home seller?

The Kansas Department of Commerce lists a 2024 county unemployment rate of 3.3% and a 2018 to 2022 median household income of $109,208.

ItemFigureSource
Population estimate, July 1, 2025636,906Census Bureau QuickFacts
Employer establishments, 202318,999Census Bureau QuickFacts
Total employment, 2023352,238Census Bureau QuickFacts
Land area473.63 square milesCensus Bureau QuickFacts
Unemployment rate, 20243.3%Kansas Department of Commerce

The state's county profile names Black & Veatch, UPS, an Amazon fulfillment center, Farmers Insurance, Zurich Insurance, AdventHealth Shawnee Mission and Johnson County Community College among the major employers.

How is a Johnson County property tax bill calculated?

The bill is assessed value times the combined mill levy, plus any special assessments, minus the school general credit. The treasurer's page gives the formula and a worked example: 23,000 assessed value x .126161 + $33 in special assessments - $172.50 credit = $2,762.20.

Assessed value is a fraction of appraised value. The county's budget guide gives the residential assessment rate as 11.5% (commercial is 25%), and one mill equals $1 for every $1,000 of assessed value.

  • County taxing district: 17.276 mills in 2025, 17.263 in the 2026 budget.
  • Library district: 3.812 mills in both years.
  • Park and recreation district: 3.018 mills in 2025, 3.020 in 2026.
  • Everything else: the city, school district and any special districts add their own levies on top of the county's total of 24.110 mills for 2025.

The school general credit was $172.50 for tax years 2024 and 2025, based on $8,625 of residential assessed value exempt from the 20 mill school general levy. Non-residential property gets no credit.

What are the key Johnson County property tax dates?

The year turns on January 1, December 20 and May 10. The Appraiser's Office values property as of January 1 and mails notices on or before March 1, and the treasurer collects in two halves.

DateWhat happens
January 1Valuation date for the appraisal year
On or before March 1Notices of Appraised Value mailed
30 days after mailingInformal appeal deadline (the county lists on or before March 31)
Mid-NovemberFirst installment notices mailed
December 20Full payment or first half due
Beginning of AprilSecond installment notices mailed
May 10Second half due
May 15 and May 20Informal real property appeals completed, and decisions mailed by May 20

The property tax division serves as both County Clerk and Treasurer. Contact it at 913-715-2600 or taxinfo@jocogov.org, or visit 111 S. Cherry St., Suite 1200, Olathe, Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

How do you appeal a Johnson County appraisal?

You get one protest per tax year, either an informal appeal in spring or a payment under protest when you pay. The Appraiser's Office says you cannot file both for the same year.

  • Informal appeal: fill out the back of the Notice of Appraised Value or use the online appeal portal, within 30 days of the mailing date.
  • Payment under protest: file with the treasurer by December 20 if you pay the tax yourself, January 31 if a mortgage company pays it, or May 10 for second half or late full payments.
  • Hearing: a 20 minute phone call, a 20 minute in-person meeting, or a review of written evidence only.
  • Next level: 30 days from the mailing date to go to the State Board of Tax Appeals, either its Small Claims Division or its Regular Division.

The appraiser must visit each property at least once every six years, using an interview, an exterior inspection and computer-generated data. A cracked foundation can pull a value down, and a finished basement can push it up, which is worth documenting before a sale. The Appeals page is at the Appraiser's Office.

What happens if Johnson County property tax goes unpaid?

Unpaid real estate tax moves from interest to publication, then a lien and finally a tax foreclosure auction. The treasurer says tax not paid by July 31 is published in the newspaper with a $15 publication fee, and on the first Tuesday in September a tax lien is placed and a redemption period begins.

If taxes remain unpaid when that period ends, the county files a foreclosure suit and the property is auctioned. A parcel can be redeemed up to 5:00 p.m. the day before the auction by paying all taxes and costs. Bidders pay in full that day, by cash or certified funds only, and anyone who owes delinquent Johnson County tax cannot bid.

The court holds a confirmation hearing four to six weeks after the auction, and the Sheriff issues a deed about 30 days after confirmation. Any surplus over the taxes and costs goes to the court. Owners who are behind and cannot sell on the open market in time sometimes look for a direct buyer instead.

What does it cost to record a deed in Johnson County?

The Register of Deeds charges $21 for the first page of a deed or mortgage and $17 for each additional page. Fees come from K.S.A. 28-115, and the office takes cash, check, money order, cashier's check or card (the card processor adds 2.25%).

  • Release of mortgage: $16 per page plus $4 per book and page.
  • Lis pendens, non-federal: $8; release of lis pendens: no charge.
  • Abstract of judgment: $17.
  • Mechanic's lien: $17.
  • Sales validation questionnaire: no charge.

Documents need a 3 inch top margin on the first page and 1 inch margins elsewhere, with type no smaller than 8 point. The office is at 111 S. Cherry St., Suite 1200, Olathe, and answers questions at 913-715-0775. A lien or judgment recorded against the house will show up in the title search, so sellers should expect to clear it at closing.

Are there tax relief programs for Johnson County homeowners?

Kansas runs three refund programs through the Department of Revenue: Homestead, SAFESR and SVR. The county says each claim must be filed with the state between January 1 and April 15 each year. They are refunds paid by the state, so they do not reduce the bill Johnson County sends in November.

If you paid the wrong parcel or paid twice, only the person who made the payment can request a refund or transfer. Requests for current-year tax are due March 15 for first-half payments and June 25 for second-half payments, and delinquent-year requests must come within 45 days of the payment date.

More questions about Johnson County, KS Property Tax Guide

When is Johnson County property tax due?

Pay in full by December 20, or in two halves: December 20 and May 10 of the next year. First notices go out in mid-November and second notices at the start of April.

How long do I have to appeal my Johnson County valuation?

You have 30 days from the date the Notice of Appraised Value was mailed, which the county lists as on or before March 31. A payment under protest has separate deadlines of December 20, January 31 or May 10.

Can I sell a Johnson County house with delinquent tax?

Yes, but the tax and interest must be cleared at or before closing. Once a parcel is on the tax foreclosure list, redemption must happen before 5:00 p.m. on the day before the auction.

Where do I record a deed in Johnson County?

At the Johnson County Register of Deeds, 111 S. Cherry St., Suite 1200, Olathe. The first page costs $21 and each added page $17.

Wyandotte County, KS Property Tax Guide: Offices, Appeals and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Kansas
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Wyandotte County, KS Property Tax Guide: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Wyandotte County, KS Property Tax Guide sale
  • Turn the Wyandotte County, KS Property Tax Guide offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling in Wyandotte County? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Wyandotte County houses as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Who to contact in Wyandotte County

  • Unified Government Treasury Division

What we confirmed on official pages

  • 2026 notices mailed Feb 25, 2026 with appeal deadline March 26, 2026; appeal deadline is the date printed on the notice
  • Appraiser does not set or collect taxes; vendor/site is the Unified Government of Wyandotte County/Kansas City, KS (wycokck.org)
  • Due dates: 1st half December 20, 2nd half May 10; delinquent after December 20; half payment allowed if total tax at least $10
  • Page states interest rate is set by statute and says 'current' rate is 12% but cites years 1998-2001, so it is stale; advertising fee added to delinquent real estate taxes
  • Informal appeal deadline is the date on the valuation notice (2026: March 26); informal meeting by May 13 (real, per page), appraiser final determination by May 20, then 30 days to file with board of tax appeals; missed deadline -> Payment Under Protest filed with Treasurer by Dec 20 (Jan 31 if escrow pays)

Tax rate

Selling in Wyandotte County?
We buy Wyandotte County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What we could not confirm

  • Valid current late-interest rate (page's 12% appears outdated)

Wyandotte County by the numbers

What is Wyandotte County and how is it laid out?

Wyandotte County is the smallest county in Kansas by area, at 156 square miles, and it shares one unified government with its county seat, Kansas City, Kansas. Wikipedia's county profile reports a 2020 population of 169,245, which makes it the fourth most populous county in the state. It was named for the Wyandot people.

The Kansas River forms part of the southern boundary, and the Missouri River lies to the east. The land rises gently from south to north, away from the rivers, and the same article notes the county receives plentiful rainfall.

Four cities sit inside the county line:

  • Kansas City, the county seat
  • Bonner Springs
  • Edwardsville
  • Lake Quivira, which also reaches into Johnson County

Inside Kansas City, the neighborhood names a seller will hear include Argentine, Armourdale, Fairfax, Rosedale, Strawberry Hill, Piper and Turner.

ItemDetailSource
Area156 square miles, smallest county in KansasWikipedia
2020 population169,245Wikipedia
Public school districtsTurner USD 202, Piper USD 203, Bonner Springs-Edwardsville USD 204, Kansas City USD 500Wikipedia
Tax due datesDecember 20 and May 10Unified Government Treasury
Residential assessment rate11.5%Unified Government Treasury

What drives the Wyandotte County economy?

The largest single retail and entertainment cluster is Village West, near the Interstate 70 and Interstate 435 interchange. It is anchored by the Kansas Speedway, and neighbors include Hollywood Casino, the Legends Outlets, Cabela's, Nebraska Furniture Mart and Great Wolf Lodge. Wikipedia says the area has fueled growth across Kansas City, Kansas.

The University of Kansas Medical Center, Kansas City Kansas Community College and Donnelly College are also based in the county. Major roads include I-35, I-70 (which doubles as the Kansas Turnpike), I-435 and I-635.

For a house seller, the useful point is that the county is small, so one appraiser and one treasurer cover every address from the river valleys to the interstate retail area. The Appraiser's own note about short housing supply is worth reading before you decide what your home might be appraised at.

What do the offices in Wyandotte County do?

The Appraiser values property, the Treasurer bills and collects, and the Unified Government publishes both services under one website. The Appraiser's page says the office does not set or collect taxes. Taxing districts do that through their budgets, which become the levy.

  • Appraiser's Office: County Annex, 8200 State Ave, Kansas City, KS 66112; phone (913) 573-8400; open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • Treasury, downtown: 710 N 7th St, Kansas City, KS 66101; phone (913) 573-2823.
  • Treasury, annex: 8200 State Ave, which also has the drop box.
  • Delinquent Real Estate: Wyandotte County Courthouse, 710 N 7th St, Suite 200; phone (913) 573-2817.

The Treasury page says payments are made online through the myWyco site or app, in person (cash, check, money order, or Visa, MasterCard and Discover), by mail with a check or money order, or in the drop box. Payments by phone are not accepted.

When is Wyandotte County property tax due?

The first half is due December 20 and the second half is due May 10. Taxes become a lien on the real estate on November 1, and about then each parcel is mailed two items: a tax bill and an information sheet that compares this year's values, rates and taxes with the year before. Parcels with a mortgage escrow get only the information sheet. Not getting a bill does not excuse late payment.

Other details from the Treasury page:

  • If the total tax is at least $10, you can pay in halves without interest.
  • A second-half bill goes out around April 1 to people who paid the first half.
  • Partial payments are accepted, but the unpaid part of the first half keeps accruing interest.
  • Parcels still unpaid on July 25 get a $16 advertising fee and are advertised in August.
  • On the first Tuesday in September, unpaid properties are "sold" to the county, which turns the taxes from current to delinquent.

The Treasury page also states an interest rate, but it cites old years, so we do not repeat it here. Call the Treasury for the current rate before you compute a payoff.

How is a Wyandotte County tax bill calculated?

The Treasury explains it in two parts: the appraiser sets value, then each taxing government sets a budget and a mill rate. Residential property is assessed at 11.5% of appraised value, and one mill is $1 of tax per $1,000 of assessed value. The page's own example is a mill levy of 70, which on an $11,500 assessed value produces $805 of tax.

Houses get a break on the school levy. The first $20,000 of a home's appraised value is not subject to the school general levy, so a $100,000 home has two assessed values: $11,500 for most levies and $9,200 for the school general levy. The state sets three levies on its own: 1 mill for educational buildings, one-half mill for correctional buildings, and 40 mills for schools.

Four school districts cover the county, which matters because each carries its own value and levy. Property inside USD 500 also supports the Kansas City, Kansas Public Library, while the rest of the county outside USD 500 and Bonner Springs pays a separate library levy.

The levy-rate PDFs linked on the Treasury page run from 2008 through 2022. For the current year, ask the Treasury or read your own statement rather than relying on an older sheet.

How do I appeal a Wyandotte County valuation?

File an informal appeal by the date printed on your valuation notice. The Appraiser's Office mailed 2026 notices on February 25 with a March 26 deadline. The Appraiser notes that most owners should expect an increase because of limited housing supply, stronger demand and revitalization in parts of the county.

Reasons the office lists for an appeal:

  • The appraised value is higher than the property could reasonably sell for.
  • The property classification is wrong.

Appeals can go in online, by hand or by mail to the Annex. Meetings can be by phone, on submitted evidence only, virtual or in person. Useful evidence includes a recent fee appraisal, photos of interior or structural problems, and recent sales of comparable properties.

One warning on the page matters a lot: if you start an informal appeal and then abandon it, you cannot pay under protest or appeal again for the same property and tax year. If you miss the deadline, the second chance is a Payment Under Protest, filed in writing with the Treasurer by December 20, or by January 31 if an escrow agent pays at least half. It cannot be used if you already appealed that year, and a first-half protest rules out a second protest for the second half.

Kansas also gives a route to the Board of Tax Appeals within 30 days of the informal decision. The state calendar on the Appraiser's page puts the informal meeting window at May 13 and the final determination at May 20.

When does Wyandotte County sell houses for unpaid tax?

The Unified Government holds two public auctions a year for tax-sale eligible property. According to the Delinquent Real Estate page, eligibility depends on the type of property:

  • Homestead properties: delinquent taxes for at least three years
  • Commercial properties: at least two years
  • Vacant and abandoned properties: at least one year

The Treasury page adds that the delinquency count starts on the first Tuesday in September of the year after the levy year, and that being eligible does not mean a parcel will be included, since only a limited number go into each sale. Delinquent payments are applied to the most recent delinquent year first, under Charter Resolution CR-01-12.

If you own a vacant or abandoned lot or house, that one-year clock is much shorter than the homestead clock, so it is worth checking the list sooner rather than later.

Can I sell a Wyandotte County house with taxes due?

Yes. Back taxes are a lien, and a title company can pay them from the sale proceeds at closing. Before you list or accept an offer, collect these items:

  1. The parcel number and a current balance from the myWyco site or the Treasury.
  2. Whether the parcel is on the tax sale list, and the date of the next auction.
  3. Any pending appeal, since abandoning one closes off a later protest.
  4. A payoff figure that runs to the closing date, because interest and the August advertising fee change the total.

Cash Home Buyers reviews Wyandotte County houses as they stand, including those with unpaid tax. You decide whether the written offer works against your payoff.

More questions about Wyandotte County, KS Property Tax Guide

Who sends the property tax bill in Wyandotte County?

The Unified Government Treasury sends it. The county Appraiser's Office values the property but does not set or collect the tax.

When is the first half of Wyandotte County property tax due?

December 20. The second half is due May 10, and halves are allowed without interest when the total tax is at least $10.

What is the Wyandotte County appeal deadline?

It is the date printed on your valuation notice. For 2026, notices were mailed February 25 and the deadline was March 26.

How long before Wyandotte County can sell a house at a tax sale?

For homestead property, the Unified Government says delinquent taxes must be at least three years old. Commercial property needs two years and vacant or abandoned property needs one.

Do Wyandotte County homeowners get a school tax break?

The Treasury page says the first $20,000 of a residence's appraised value is not subject to the school general levy, so a house carries two assessed values.

Who to contact in Pottawatomie County

Tax rate

Selling in Pottawatomie County?
We buy Pottawatomie County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Where is Pottawatomie County, Kansas, and what does it cover?

Pottawatomie County sits in northeastern Kansas and covers 862 square miles, of which 841 are land. The Pottawatomie County Economic Development Corporation describes it as lying between Manhattan and Topeka, with Westmoreland as the county seat and Wamego as the largest city.

Territorial lawmakers created the county in 1857 out of land that had belonged to Riley County. The county's own history page says the seat started at St. George, moved to Louisville after the 1861 election, and later moved again. Wikipedia dates the vote that chose Westmoreland to 1882.

ItemDetailSource
Land and water area862 sq mi total, 841 land, 21 water (2.4%)Pottawatomie County Economic Development Corporation
County seatWestmorelandWikipedia, county page
2020 census population25,348Wikipedia, citing the Census Bureau
2025 population estimate27,186Wikipedia, county page
OrganizedFebruary 20, 1857Wikipedia, county page
NeighborsMarshall, Nemaha, Jackson, Shawnee, Wabaunsee and Riley countiesWikipedia, county page

For a seller, the practical point is that the county is mostly farmland dotted with small towns. Your tax bill depends on the city and school district your parcel falls into.

Which towns and school districts matter for a Pottawatomie County house sale?

The county's cities are Belvue, Emmett, Havensville, Louisville, Manhattan, Olsburg, Onaga, St. George, St. Marys, Wamego, Westmoreland and Wheaton. Manhattan and St. Marys also extend into adjacent counties. Wamego had 4,841 residents in the 2020 census, according to Wikipedia, and sits where U.S. 24 meets K-99, roughly 14 miles east of Manhattan.

Four unified districts are based in the county: Wamego USD 320, Kaw Valley USD 321, Onaga USD 322 and Rock Creek USD 323. Wikipedia also lists districts with offices in neighboring counties, including Manhattan-Ogden USD 383, so confirm the district for your parcel on your tax statement.

  • Wamego is known for its Oz Museum and a Dutch Mill built in 1879 in the city park.
  • St. Marys has a private academy and college, listed on the county page.
  • Green Valley, near Manhattan, carries a Manhattan mailing address although it is outside the city limits, as the county explains on its FAQ.

That last point catches sellers off guard. A house with a Manhattan address in Green Valley is taxed, permitted and inspected by county rules, not by the City of Manhattan.

What is the local economy like, and how does it affect sellers?

The county's development corporation says much of the county is agricultural land and its leading industries include manufacturing, trade, transport and utilities, healthcare and private education. It puts the county labor force at roughly 12,400 at the end of 2022 and projects the population to pass 36,000 by 2044.

Growth in a rural county matters to a seller. The same corporation calls Pottawatomie County an exception among rural Kansas counties because it kept adding residents while many others lost them. The corporation also points to the county's position between Manhattan and Topeka and its proximity to institutions such as Kansas State University.

The development corporation publishes quarterly economic reviews that track home sales, building permits and sales tax revenue. Those reports are worth a look if you want local numbers before you decide how to sell.

How does Pottawatomie County value property and send out notices?

The County Appraiser lists and values every parcel, and notices of value for real property go out by March 1. The county FAQ says state law requires the appraiser to view and inspect all property once every six years, though inspections can happen more often.

The appraiser does not simply use what you paid. The county says one sale carries weight but the appraiser has to decide whether it was an arm's length deal, then compare similar sales. Appraisals are set as of January 1 each year, so a house you bought in the summer is still valued against that earlier date.

A higher value does not automatically raise your bill. The county explains that the amount you owe depends on the budgets of the local governments that tax your parcel, special assessments, and the state school levy. The County Clerk divides each unit's budget need by the assessed value in its area to arrive at the mill levy, then certifies the tax roll to the Treasurer.

How do you appeal a Pottawatomie County valuation?

You contact the County Appraiser's Office within 30 days of the date the notice was mailed. The county's tax calendar lists the informal meeting deadline as May 15, with Hearing Officer or Panel hearings finished by July 1.

There is a second route. You can file a payment under protest form with the County Treasurer when you pay, no later than December 20. If an escrow or tax service agent pays for you by that date, the filing deadline moves to January 31. Pottawatomie County warns that once you appeal the notice of value, you cannot pay under protest for the same parcel and year, so pick one path.

  • Ask the appraiser for the Property Record Card and check bedrooms, baths and square footage.
  • Request the comparable sales sheet, which lists up to five similar homes.
  • Bring photos, repair estimates for structural damage, a recent fee appraisal or a sales contract from the last two to three years.
  • If a non-attorney will speak for you, complete the Declaration of Representation form.

At a small claims hearing run by the State Board of Tax Appeals, the county has to prove its value is right, according to the county FAQ.

When are Pottawatomie County property taxes due?

The first half, or the full amount, is due on or before December 20, and the second half is due by May 10 of the following year.

StepDate
Valuation notices mailedBy March 1
Informal meeting with County AppraiserMay 15
Hearing Officer or Panel hearingsJuly 1
First half or full paymentDecember 20
Second halfMay 10 of the next year

These dates come from the county's Tax Calendar page and treasurer information.

Who pays the tax when a Pottawatomie County house sells mid-year?

Unless the contract says otherwise, the buyer owes the tax on real property sold on or after January 1 and before November 1, and the seller owes it if the sale closes on or after November 1 and before January 1. The county cites K.S.A. 79-1805 for that rule.

The same FAQ says property is not prorated on the tax roll when it changes hands (K.S.A. 79-309). Many purchase contracts prorate anyway, which is why a settlement statement often shows a credit or a charge for taxes. A cash buyer and a seller can agree on this in writing, and the county treats the private contract as controlling.

If you sell around November or December, look at the timing closely. Under the default rule a seller who closes in late November owes that year's bill, and the December 20 deadline is only weeks away.

What building and land rules affect a Pottawatomie County property?

County building codes apply only inside the Blue Township Sewer District, which includes Green Valley, and have applied there since January 1, 2020. Outside that district, the county says it is the buyer's job to check the quality of construction.

Zoning is also unusual. When countywide zoning started in 1972, nearly all of the county was zoned A1, agriculture, so even a single-family home can require a rezoning. For rural lots, the county's rule of thumb is a minimum of 3 acres with a rural or city water district and a private septic system, or 5 acres with a private well and septic.

  • A permit is needed for houses, additions, moved-in homes and manufactured homes; sheds of 120 square feet or less and fences do not need one.
  • Any type of manufactured home may go on an operating farm of 40 acres or more for the owner, a blood relative or an employee.
  • Rural burn permits apply only in unincorporated areas; cities such as Wamego and Westmoreland follow their own rules.
  • Green Valley has no adopted nuisance code, so overgrown grass or noise are not covered by county resolutions.

How are deeds and liens handled at the Pottawatomie County Register of Deeds?

Documents are recorded the same day the Register of Deeds receives them, once the office has checked them for completeness, assessed the fee and scanned them. No document is filed until the fee is paid.

The office also holds many liens, including UCC filings and federal and state tax liens, but not all of them. The county advises checking with the Clerk of the District Court and the Kansas Department of Revenue for others. The Register of Deeds is also the office to call about restrictive covenants in a subdivision.

Before closing, pull the title history, confirm special assessments with the county Administration Office, and settle any lien you find.

What sellers in Pottawatomie County usually face

Based on the county rules above, the issues to plan for are private wells and septic systems, agricultural zoning, a school district that may differ from the mailing address, and closing dates that fall near the December 20 and May 10 payment dates.

  • Inherited farmhouses where the title is not yet clear.
  • Manufactured homes that were placed under older county rules.
  • Green Valley houses that carry a Manhattan address but follow county rules.
  • Owners who missed the 30-day appeal window and want to know what comes next.

If one of these fits your house, you can send us the address and we will explain how a cash sale would work.

More questions about Pottawatomie County, KS Property Tax Guide

Who do I call about a Pottawatomie County valuation?

Call the Pottawatomie County Appraiser's Office within 30 days of the mailing date printed on your notice. The County Treasurer handles payment under protest and the bill itself.

Does Pottawatomie County prorate property tax at closing?

No, not on the tax roll. The county says property is not prorated off or onto the roll, though private contracts commonly prorate. Check your sales contract to see who owes what.

What is the deadline to pay Pottawatomie County property tax?

The first half or the full amount is due December 20, and the second half is due May 10 of the following year. Missing December 20 can make the whole bill due.

Can I sell a house in Pottawatomie County with taxes still owed?

Yes. Unpaid taxes become a lien that is cleared at closing from the proceeds, so the buyer receives clean title. Confirm the balance with the Treasurer before you set a closing date.

Do county building codes apply to every Pottawatomie County house?

No. The county has adopted building codes only inside the Blue Township Sewer District. Elsewhere in the county, the buyer is responsible for checking construction quality.

Where is Sumner County, Kansas, and what towns does it include?

Sumner County is in south-central Kansas, directly south of Sedgwick County and bordering Oklahoma, with Wellington as the county seat and largest city. It covers 1,185 square miles, of which 1,182 are land, and the 2020 census counted 22,382 residents.

The county was organized in 1870 and is named for U.S. Senator Charles Sumner of Massachusetts. Its incorporated cities are Argonia, Belle Plaine, Caldwell, Conway Springs, Geuda Springs, Hunnewell, Mayfield, Milan, Mulvane, Oxford, South Haven and Wellington. Mulvane and Geuda Springs extend into neighboring counties. Beyond those are small unincorporated communities and 30 townships, which matters because township and special-district levies change a rural bill.

FactDetail
County seatWellington
Area1,185 square miles
2020 census population22,382
Courthouse501 N. Washington, Wellington, KS 67152
Register of Deeds phone(620) 326-2041

What does the Sumner County economy rely on?

Farming, local government and schools, and a handful of manufacturers carry much of the county. The Kansas Department of Agriculture, using the 2022 Census of Agriculture, reports 1,013 farms on 750,650 acres in Sumner County, with $182 million in crop and livestock sales that year.

The Greater Wichita Partnership's regional snapshot names Sumner County, Wellington USD 353 and Triumph Group as major employers. The county also sits next to the Wichita job market, and the Kansas Turnpike has an exit near Mulvane. The Kansas Star Casino opened in December 2011 about 4.5 miles west of Mulvane, next to a turnpike exit.

For a seller, this means two kinds of Sumner County property sale. A town house in Wellington or Mulvane often attracts commuters, while an acreage or farm house near Caldwell or Argonia draws a smaller, more specialized group of buyers.

Which school districts cover Sumner County houses?

Twelve unified school districts reach into the county, and the one that serves a parcel sets a large part of its tax bill. The districts are Mulvane USD 263, Clearwater USD 264, Kingman-Norwich USD 331, Wellington USD 353, Conway Springs USD 356, Belle Plaine USD 357, Oxford USD 358, Argonia USD 359, Caldwell USD 360, South Haven USD 509, Arkansas City USD 470 and Udall USD 463.

The county clerk's 2025 levy sheet shows how much the district choice matters. Total school levies range from 43.329 mills for the Arkansas City district to 74.411 mills for Caldwell, and Wellington sits at 50.863. Two houses of similar value can carry noticeably different bills only because of where the district line runs.

How large is a Sumner County property tax bill?

The county clerk's certified 2025 levy sheet shows a combined county and state levy of 51.537 mills on every parcel, before city, township, school and special-district levies are added. The county levy is 50.037 mills and the state levy is 1.500 mills.

The sheet lists a total levy for each city, which already includes the state, county, school, township and other layers for that location:

City (2025 total levy, mills)Total
Wellington169.563
Mulvane172.621
Oxford163.538
South Haven169.839
Belle Plaine189.460
Caldwell245.767
Argonia162.099

Rural parcels have their own tax-unit codes. For example, a township parcel in the Wellington school district near Wellington Township carries 139.157 mills, while a parcel in Morris Township in the Caldwell school district carries 245.821. Find your parcel's tax-unit code on the tax statement and match it to the county's levy sheet page.

How does the Sumner County Appraiser value a house?

The appraiser values every parcel as of January 1 at fair market value, using the cost approach and the sales approach for residential property. The county's explanation page says the income approach is not used for residences in Sumner County because there is not enough data to apply it efficiently.

It cites the Kansas definition of fair market value as the amount a well-informed buyer is justified in paying and a well-informed seller is justified in accepting in an open and competitive market, without undue compulsion. The county also says its appraisals are tested against statute, and a variance of 10% above or below market value is not treated as a violation under K.S.A. 79-1426.

Disasters get a specific rule. If a house burns or is damaged by a tornado, wind, flood or vandalism, the county says it is still valued as it stood on January 1 of the tax year, even if the damage happened on January 2, and the tax is not due until December 20. A seller who sells a storm-damaged house mid-year should expect that the bill reflects the earlier condition.

What are the Sumner County appraisal dates and appeal steps?

Real estate valuation notices go out March 1, real property appeals are due March 30, and informal conferences finish by May 15 with decisions mailed by May 20. The county appraiser's tax calendar lists the full schedule.

  • January 1: valuation date for real and personal property.
  • March 1: real estate valuation notices mailed.
  • March 30: deadline to file real property appeals.
  • May 15: informal valuation conferences completed, and personal property appeals due.
  • June 15: appraiser certifies the roll to the county clerk.
  • Dec 20: first-half payment under protest deadline.

The county advises appealing if you could not sell the house for the value shown, and says you may appeal once a year, either after the notice or when you pay the tax. Bring photographs of damage, sales of similar properties and a list of questions. The appraiser's page also says sales information is open to the public from March 31 through May 15 for owners considering an appeal.

How do deed and estate records get filed in Sumner County?

The Sumner County Register of Deeds, on the first floor of the courthouse in Wellington, records every real estate transaction in the county. Its FAQ lists $21.00 for the first page of a deed, mortgage, oil and gas lease, affidavit or death certificate and $17.00 for each additional page.

A mortgage release or assignment costs $20.00 for the first page that releases one book and page, plus $4.00 for each extra page, and an extra $16.00 applies for each additional book and page released in the same document. Those details matter when an estate sells a house, because a death certificate or affidavit often goes into the record alongside the deed. The office also refers customers to local title companies for title insurance or abstract updates.

What do Sumner County sellers commonly face?

Rural and small-town sellers deal with inherited houses, farm parcels with outbuildings, and storm damage. A cash buyer can skip the appraisal and repair negotiation that tend to stall those sales.

  • Different levies: a rural tax unit can carry a much higher total than a Wellington address.
  • Estate records: collect the death certificate, any affidavits and the deed before you call anyone.
  • Storm damage: the appraiser values the property as of January 1, so keep photographs and repair estimates.
  • Payment timing: December 20 and May 10 are the two tax dates to plan a closing around.

Sumner County is close to Wichita, but its offices, tax rolls and levy rules are separate from Sedgwick County, so use Sumner's own pages for your parcel.

More questions about Sumner County, KS Property Tax Guide

What is the county seat of Sumner County, Kansas?

The county seat is Wellington, which is also the largest city. The courthouse is at 501 N. Washington in Wellington.

What is the Sumner County mill levy?

The 2025 county levy is 50.037 mills and the state levy is 1.500 mills, for 51.537 combined. City, school, township and special-district levies are added on top, so total rates by city in 2025 range from 162.099 mills in Argonia to 245.767 in Caldwell.

When is the deadline to appeal a Sumner County valuation?

March 30 is the deadline to file real property appeals, according to the county appraiser's tax calendar. Informal conferences are completed by May 15, and decisions are mailed by May 20.

How much does it cost to record a deed in Sumner County?

The Register of Deeds lists $21.00 for the first page and $17.00 for each additional page. The same fee applies to mortgages, affidavits and death certificates.

Is a damaged house valued lower in Sumner County?

Not for the current tax year. The county says a property damaged by fire, tornado, wind, flood or vandalism is still valued as it stood on January 1, even if the damage happens the next day.

Which school district is my Sumner County house in?

It depends on the parcel. Twelve districts reach into the county, including Wellington USD 353, Mulvane USD 263 and Caldwell USD 360, and your tax statement's unit code shows which one applies.
